Overview: each tool answers one question
Orderflow is not about watching as much as possible. Each tool is used at a specific moment as price approaches a key level drawn from TPO.
Who is waiting where? Limit orders resting at each price, holding or being pulled.

Aggressive buying minus aggressive selling within one candle. Compare with the candle direction to see agreement or absorption.

Where it is worth trading, and whether to fade or break. Not orderflow, but it decides whether orderflow means anything.

Foundations: market orders, limit orders and the auction
Every orderflow tool measures one of two things: resting orders (passive) or orders filled by the aggressive side (aggressive).
is reading the actual flow of orders being filled and resting to see which side controls price at a specific level, instead of only looking at the result, the candle.
Limit order = passive
Rests at a price, waiting for someone else to fill it. Buy limits sit on the bid, sell limits on the ask. Shown on the DOM. Can be pulled at any time, so it can be a spoof.
Market order = aggressor
Accepts the other side’s price to fill immediately. Market buys fill on the ask, market sells fill on the bid. Shown on the tape and footprint after the fill.
How price moves
Price only ticks up when all sell limits at the current ask are eaten by market buys, or pulled by whoever placed them.
So market orders are the side that
creates movement
, limit orders are the side that
blocks it or lets it through
Heavy market buying without price rising means a large sell limit is absorbing: this is the root of the absorption concept.
Price moves fast through areas with few resting orders (LVN) and slows down in areas with many orders and much volume (HVN). This is the link between orderflow and TPO/volume profile.
Two kinds of activity in Auction Market Theory
The aggressive side pushes price out of the value area and it gets accepted. Orderflow: stacked imbalance, CVD confirms, fast tape. Fits the playbook
Price leaves value and gets pushed back. Orderflow: absorption, exhaustion, divergence, delta flip. Fits the playbook
Quick check · Foundations
DOM: the order book
ATAS: Smart DOM. Used in phase 3 when price touches the level.

shows the number of limit contracts resting at each price around the current price: the bid side (resting buys) and the ask side (resting sells). The DOM shows passive liquidity, not trades that have happened.
Concepts
Resting orders added at a price as price approaches. Someone wants to defend that level.
Resting orders pulled just before price touches. An open road for price to pass.
Wall
A price with unusually large size compared with its neighbours. Only meaningful when volume trades into it and it still stands.
A large order placed to create an impression, then pulled before it is filled. The reason not to trust the DOM alone.
An order that shows only part of its size. Volume traded at the price far exceeds the displayed size, and the size keeps refilling.
DOM history over time (ATAS: DOM Levels). Shows how long a wall has existed and whether it was pulled before price arrived.
How to read
Only watch the DOM when price is a few ticks from the chosen level. Do not use the DOM to find setups.
Compare size at the level with when price was far away: an increase is stacking, a decrease without traded volume is pulling.
Cross-check with the tape: size decreasing
because of fills
(the wall being eaten) is completely different from size decreasing
because of pulling
Watch the opposite side too: a long fade needs the ask above to thin out; a long break needs the bid below to follow price up.

C. Iceberg on the bid

The DOM always shows 12 lots at 25,410.50 but the tape shows 186 lots traded at this price and price has not broken. A large player is absorbing with a hidden order. An iceberg at an extreme usually holds price; an iceberg that gets broken usually leads to a strong move in the break direction.

Always confirm with the tape: are there real fills?
Note whether the opposite side is thin or thick.

Presence = time spent at a price (TPO). Participation = volume actually traded at a price (volume profile).
Thick TPO + thin volume = present but few participants: weak value. Thin TPO + thick volume = big business passing quickly: a strong level.
This is why your template puts TPO and volume profile side by side. Prefer levels that both confirm.
TPOC = the price with the most TPOs (time). VPOC = the price with the most volume. Usually close to each other but not necessarily.
The POC is the
fairest

Yesterday’s POC is the natural target of every rotation inside the VA. A POC not yet revisited = naked POC, a magnet.
The area holding ~70% of TPOs (or volume) around the POC. Upper edge VAH, lower edge VAL.
Inside the VA = fair value, both sides agree. Outside the VA = an
unfair

The range of A + B, i.e. 9:30–10:30 ET. IB width = IB High − IB Low.
An IB narrow versus average = the two sides have not agreed yet, a strong range extension is likely. A wide IB = most of the day’s range is in, leaning to rotation.
The IB is the anchor of the IB model you use. Compare IB width with the 20-session average (tool in tab 03).

On the footprint, what is the number in the ask column?
Sell limit orders resting at that price
Volume filled by aggressive buyers into the ask
Volume filled by aggressive sellers into the ask

The ask on the footprint is volume filled when market buy orders hit the ask side. Resting limit orders only appear on the DOM.
Who is the aggressor?
The side placing the largest limit order
The side using market orders, accepting the other side’s price
The side currently in profit
The aggressor fills immediately with market orders. The side placing limits is passive.
When does NQ tick up by one tick?
When there are more buy limits than sell limits
When all sell orders at the current ask are eaten or pulled
When delta is positive
When CVD rises
Price only moves to the next ask level when the current ask has no orders left: fully filled or pulled. So heavy market buying with price standing still is a sign of absorption.
Price leaves value and is pushed back inside with absorption and divergence. What kind of activity is this?
Responsive is the reaction pushing price back to value. The matching playbook is Fade.
What is stacking on the DOM?
Resting orders pulled as price approaches
Resting orders added at a price as price approaches
Many market orders filling at once

Stacking shows someone wants to defend that price. Confusing it with stacked imbalance (footprint) is a common mistake.
A 400-lot ask wall above. As price approaches, the size drops 400 → 120 and the tape shows buy orders filling continuously at that price. How do you read it?
Spoof, about to be pulled
The wall is really being eaten, a break is likely
The wall holds, short it
No information
Size dropping because of fills (volume on the tape) means buyers are eating the liquidity. Unlike pulling, where size drops without traded volume.
